memory_candidates.content: A jq invocation that references only --argjson/--slurpfile variables (no `.` on stdin) MUST still pass -n (null input). Without -n, jq blocks on/reads an empty stdin and silently emits ZERO output with exit 0 -- no error, just an empty result that propagates as an empty variable through `set -uo pipefail` scripts (no -e), making the bug very easy to miss in code review since the script 'runs successfully'. Always pass -n whenever a jq filter's only inputs are --argjson/--arg/--slurpfile bindings.

When a live dispatch path and a read-only preview/dry-run path must agree on a routing rule (e.g. task-status -> next-action), extract the rule into its own script taking an explicit mode/engine argument rather than letting the preview reimplement or approximate the live logic. Both callers invoke the SAME script; a genuine behavioral fork (e.g. single-task vs multi-task engines disagreeing on one edge case) is then represented as an explicit engine argument and asserted by a fixture test, not silently papered over. This is the 'one code path, two consumers' pattern.
